docs.title: Intervention Grammar
docs.text:
A grammar of interventions in existing structures.

A structure is a set of members and their connections. Operators change it: they cut, split, join, remove and add members, change the shape of a joint, release and secure connections, lift and prop, and record what is found. Approaches compose operators into interventions: repairs, reinforcements, additions and alterations. A program of operations runs on a model, step by step, and every step can be undone.

The demo wall after an inspection. The foot of post_3 is damaged (red ring).

After a prosthesis. The foot is cut off, a new piece (black ring) is joined to the post and rests on the sill.

Each box is a member, coloured by its role. An arrow points from a member to the member it rests on, down to the ground.

The operators describe what is done to a structure, independent of who does it: a person, a robot or a program carry out the same Split or Lift. They are independent of the material as well. Operators that work along a member (Split, Trim, Extend, Turn, Machine) measure positions in stations along its axis, so the grammar suits frames and trusses of linear members first.

The structure is a compas_model Model, and the state of the intervention lives on its graph. The same operations therefore run on any compas_model element, for example the beams of a compas_timber model. Every operation is a COMPAS Data class and saves and loads as JSON.

from intervention_grammar import demo, run, inverse
from intervention_grammar import Probe, Prosthesis

wall = demo.wall()
program = [
    Probe("post_3", at=0.1, finding="damaged"),
    Prosthesis("post_3", length=0.4, joint={"family": "lap", "length": 0.3}),
]
states = run(wall, program)    # every state, step by step
undo = inverse(wall, program)  # the program that undoes it

Start with the concepts, look up the operators and approaches, or follow the examples. The drawings on this page are made with graph_drawing.

Intervention Grammar is developed by Tizian Rein at the Professorship of Digital Fabrication, Technical University of Munich.

docs.title: Approaches
docs.text:
An approach is an operation made of other operations. When a program runs, each approach is expanded into its operators for the model as it is at that moment, and each operator is checked and applied in turn. The log lists the operators, so a program of approaches and its expansion can always be compared.

Approach Parameters What it does Steps Patch member, region, piece, joint Cut damaged material out of part of a member and fit a new piece. Cut ; Inlay ; Secure Prosthesis member, length, end, joint, zone, path Replace a member over its full section along a length at one end. Release ; Split ; Remove the old end ; Add ; Insert ; Seat ; Join ; Secure MidProsthesis member, span, joints, zone, path Replace a member over its full section along a length in its middle. as Prosthesis, with two joints Replacement member, new, path Replace a whole member. Release ; Withdraw ; Remove ; Add ; Insert ; Seat ; Join ; Secure Reinforcement member, piece, face, span, joint Add a piece alongside a member and fasten the two together; the piece shares the member's load path. Double ; Secure Addition member, between, type, joint, length Introduce a new member that takes part of the load; the damage stays. Cut ; Add ; Secure Reconnection member, other Remake a failed connection with a separate connector. Release ; Cut ; Detach ; Secure Realignment members, by Move members back into line and secure them again. Release ; Move ; Secure Subtraction member, region Take damaged or harmful material away without replacing it. Cut, or Release ; Remove Repositioning member, mode, quarter, path Take a member out, turn it, and put it back, so that its damaged parts lie where they matter less. Release ; Withdraw ; Turn ; Inlay the old cuts ; Cut new ones ; Insert ; Seat ; Secure Collapse remove, ring, rest, by, joint Remove a bay and close the structure up (an edge ring collapse). Remove the members of a bay ; Split and Remove the bay segments ; Move the rest ; Join ; Secure Bypass member, through, to, end, by, at Remove a member and let a neighbour that ended on it continue to the next member. Extend ; Reroute ; Remove ; Secure Lowering standing, base, above, by Shorten the members standing on a base, replace the base and lower everything above onto it. Prop ; Remove the base ; Trim the standing members ; new base in ; Move down ; Join ; Secure ; Unprop Retain member, note Leave the structure as it is and record why: the baseline every other approach is compared with. Record

Where an approach needs the connections in a zone of a member, it reads their stations, or takes them from its zone parameter.

Retain changes nothing and records why. It is the baseline every other approach is compared with, the minimum intervention.

docs.title: Writing an approach
docs.text:
A new approach is a subclass of Approach with its parameters, __data__ for saving it, and operations(model), which returns the operations in the order they are carried out:

from intervention_grammar import Approach, Release, Withdraw, Turn, Insert, Seat, Secure
from intervention_grammar.state import neighbours


class TurnAround(Approach):
    """Take a member out, turn it end for end, and put it back."""

    def __init__(self, member):
        super(TurnAround, self).__init__()
        self.member = member

    @property
    def __data__(self):
        return {"member": self.member}

    def operations(self, model):
        others = neighbours(model, self.member)
        return (
            [Release(self.member, o) for o in others]
            + [Withdraw(self.member), Turn(self.member, mode="end"), Insert(self.member), Seat(self.member)]
            + [Secure(self.member, o) for o in others]
        )

check and inverse come with the base class: an approach can be applied if all its operators can, and its inverse is the inverse of its operators in reverse order.

docs.title: State
docs.text:
A structure is a compas_model Model: members are elements, connections are interactions. The state of the intervention lives on the model's graph, one set of attributes per element node and one per connection edge. Element classes stay untouched, so the same operations run on any compas_model element.

Element attribute Values fabric "original" or "new" condition "sound" or "damaged" placement "in", "inserted" (in place, not yet seated), "out" (taken out, kept) or "missing" (known, not there) type the role of the member, any name grounded True if it stands on the ground length in metres, if known trim change of length at each end, {"start": d, "end": d} turn end for end, and quarter turns about the axis offset sum of the moves, [x, y, z] lift how far it is jacked up props stations of temporary props cuts regions cut out of it ends joints machined into its ends fills ends filled with new material after machining findings results of probes notes records exposed True while it is opened up log numbers of the steps that changed it Connection attribute Values joint family and parameters, a plain dict state "secured", "released" or "open" (made, not yet fastened) at station on each member, {name: metres} node the point where it meets other connections support (carried, carrier) or "both", if known

All operators change the model through a few basic edits in intervention_grammar.state: add or remove an element, add or remove a connection, set an attribute on either. Another kind of model needs only that module translated.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
Every operator is a COMPAS Data class with three methods:

  • check(model) raises an InterventionError if the operation cannot be applied to the model as it is,
  • apply(model) changes the model,
  • inverse(model) returns the operation that undoes it, given the model before it was applied.

An operation saves and loads with compas.json_dump and compas.json_load, so a program can be written, stored and exchanged as JSON.

docs.title: Approach
docs.text: An Approach is an operation made of other operations. It is expanded step by step when it runs, for the model as it is at that moment. See Approaches.

docs.title: Program
docs.text: A program is a plain list of operations and approaches. run(model, program) applies it to a copy of the model and returns every state: the model before the first step and after each step. Each state carries the log of all steps so far in model.graph.attributes["log"]. inverse(model, program) gives the program that undoes it.

docs.title: Levels
docs.text: The grammar says what changes in a structure. How the steps are ordered and assigned to people and machines, and how a robot carries them out, are separate levels, kept in other packages. A program and its states can be handed to them.

docs.title: What is checked
docs.text:
check asks whether an operation fits the state: the member exists, a connection is secured before it can be released, a member held by secured connections cannot be withdrawn or moved, a connection can only be secured once both members are in place, a member is out before it is turned, a trim does not cut through a connection, a split lies inside the member.

Not checked: whether a member can physically move along its path, support and statics, tool access. These need geometry and are outside the scope of this package. Without geometry, volumes are unknown, so original_share weighs members by length.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: The examples use demo.wall, a timber wall of two bays without geometry: a sill and a plate over both bays, three posts, two rails and two braces, all joints secured.

docs.title: A prosthesis
docs.text:
The foot of post_3 is found damaged. A prosthesis cuts the post through above the damage, removes the old foot and joins a new piece to the post and to the sill.

from intervention_grammar import demo, run, inverse, original_share
from intervention_grammar import Probe, Prosthesis

wall = demo.wall()
program = [
    Probe("post_3", at=0.1, finding="damaged"),
    Prosthesis("post_3", length=0.4, joint={"family": "lap", "length": 0.3}),
]

states = run(wall, program)
for entry in states[-1].graph.attributes["log"]:
    print(entry["step"], entry["text"])

The approach expands into the operators it is made of:

 1  Probe(member='post_3', at=0.1, finding='damaged')
 2  Release(a='post_3', b='sill')
 3  Split(member='post_3', at=0.4, joint={'family': 'lap', 'length': 0.3}, pieces=['post_3.old', 'post_3'])
 4  Remove(member='post_3.old')
 5  Add(member='post_3.new', placed=False, attributes={'type': 'post', 'length': 0.4, 'grounded': False})
 6  Insert(member='post_3.new', path='straight')
 7  Seat(member='post_3.new')
 8  Join(a='post_3.new', b='post_3', joint={'family': 'lap', 'length': 0.3}, state='open', at={'post_3.new': 0.4, 'post_3': 0})
 9  Join(a='post_3.new', b='sill', joint={'family': 'tenon'}, state='open', at={'sill': 2.9, 'post_3.new': 0}, support=['post_3.new', 'sill'])
10  Secure(a='post_3.new', b='post_3')
11  Secure(a='post_3.new', b='sill')

states holds twelve models: the wall before the first step and after each of the eleven steps. original_share(states[-1]) gives 97.7 %, the share of the wall that is still original material, weighed by length.

docs.title: Undoing it
docs.text:
for op in inverse(wall, program):
    print(op)

Release(a='post_3.new', b='sill')
Release(a='post_3.new', b='post_3')
Unjoin(a='post_3.new', b='sill')
Unjoin(a='post_3.new', b='post_3')
Unseat(member='post_3.new')
Withdraw(member='post_3.new', path='straight')
Remove(member='post_3.new')
Add(member='post_3.old', element=<Element post_3.old>, placed=True, connections={...}, attributes={...})
Merge(a='post_3.old', b='post_3', into='post_3')
Secure(a='post_3', b='sill')

The inverse brings the structure back to its shape. The old foot returns as the element it was, with its condition and findings; the probe has no inverse, since what was learned stays known.

docs.title: When an operation does not fit
docs.text:
run checks every step before it applies it, and stops at the first one that does not fit the state:

from intervention_grammar import InterventionError, Withdraw

try:
    run(wall, [Withdraw("post_3")])
except InterventionError as error:
    print(error)

step 1, Withdraw(member='post_3', path='straight'): post_3 is still held by secured joints with sill, plate, rail_2

docs.title: Saving a program
docs.text:
Operations are COMPAS Data, so a program and every state save and load as JSON:

import compas

compas.json_dump(program, "program.json")
program = compas.json_load("program.json")

docs.title: Drawing the states
docs.text:
graph_drawing draws a model with its state as a graph: members as boxes coloured by type, arrows from the carried member to the carrying one, rings for damaged and new members. The drawings on the home page are made with it:

from graph_drawing import models

drawing = models.drawing(states[-1], title="after the prosthesis")
with open("after.svg", "w") as f:
    f.write(drawing.to_svg())
drawing.to_pdf("after.pdf")

docs.title: In Grasshopper
docs.text:
rhino/run_program.py is the body of a Python 3 Script component. Its input program takes operation objects or text, one operation per item:

Probe("post_3", at=0.1, finding="damaged")
Prosthesis("post_3", length=0.4, joint={"family": "lap", "length": 0.3})

The outputs are every state, one chosen state, the log and the error.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Intervention Grammar needs Python 3.9 or newer, COMPAS 2.15.1 or newer and compas_model 0.9.2 or newer, below 0.10. compas_timber 2.2 requires compas_model 0.9.2, so the two packages share one environment.

docs.title: User
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install it into your environment:

git clone https://github.com/augmentedfabricationlab/intervention_grammar.git
pip install -e intervention_grammar

Check the installation:

python -c "import intervention_grammar; print(intervention_grammar.__version__)"

docs.title: Rhino 8 and Grasshopper
docs.text:
Rhino 8 runs Python 3.9. Find its Python with

python -m compas_rhino.print_python_path

and install the package there as well:

path/to/rhino/python -m pip install -e intervention_grammar

Or open any Python 3 script in Rhino 8, go to Tools, Options in the script editor and add the src folder of the repository to the Python path. compas_model has to be installed in Rhino's Python in that case.

rhino/run_program.py is the body of a Python 3 Script component in Grasshopper. It runs a program on a model and outputs every state, one chosen state, the log and the error. The program is a list of operation objects or of text such as Prosthesis("post_3", length=0.4).

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Every operator is a class with check, apply and inverse. The operators fall into four layers. Structure operators change what the finished structure is. Joint operators change the shape of a connection. Process operators move the structure through temporary states on the way. Knowledge operators change what is known about it.

Members and connections are named by the names of their elements: a connection is given by its two members a and b. Positions along a member are stations, in metres from its start.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
What the finished structure is: its members, their connections, their lengths and their positions.

Operator Parameters What it does Inverse Cut member, region Cut material out of a member. Inlay Inlay member, piece, region, joint Fit a new piece into a member. Remove of the piece Split member, at, joint, pieces, start Cut a member through at a station; the two pieces meet in a joint. Merge Join a, b, joint, state, at, support Join two members with a joint. Unjoin Unjoin a, b Take away the connection between two members. Join Merge a, b, into Make two connected pieces one member again. Split Trim member, end, by Shorten a member at one end. Extend Extend member, end, by Lengthen a member at one end. Trim Turn member, mode, quarter Turn a member that is out: end for end, or about its own axis. Turn in the opposite direction Add member, like, element, placed, connections, attributes Add a member to the structure. Remove Remove member Take a member out of the structure for good; its connections go with it. Add Double member, piece, face, span, joint Add a piece alongside a member, sharing its load path. Remove of the piece Support member, at, support, kind Give a member a permanent support from the ground. Remove of the support Reroute member, old, new, at, state Connect a member to another one instead. Reroute to the old member SplitNode node, connections, new Let some connections of a crowded node meet in a node of their own. MergeNodes MergeNodes node, other Let the connections of two nodes meet in one. SplitNode Move members, by Move members permanently. Move by the opposite vector Swap a, b Two members that are out exchange their places in the structure. Swap

Remove is undone geometrically: the member comes back in its shape, in new material. The same holds for Cut, which an inlay undoes, and for Fill. The share of original material that remains is measured with original_share.

docs.title: Joint
docs.text:
The shape of a connection. Joints are plain dicts, a family name and its parameters, for example {"family": "lap", "length": 0.3}. The grammar stores and changes them and leaves the meaning of a family to the tools that make or check the joint, so joints can come from any source.

Operator Parameters What it does Inverse Select a, b, joint Set the joint of a connection. Select with the previous joint Orient a, b, turns Turn the joint about the member axis by quarter turns. Orient by the opposite number of turns Tilt a, b, angle, plane Tilt a cutting plane of the joint by an angle. Tilt by the opposite angle Lengthen a, b, by Make the joint longer. Shorten Shorten a, b, by Make the joint shorter. Lengthen Mirror a, b Mirror the joint. Mirror AddFeature a, b, feature Add a feature to the joint. Select with the joint as it was Fasten a, b, fastener, count Add fasteners to the joint. Select with the joint as it was Detach a, b Make the connecting part of a joint a separate piece. Select with the joint as it was Open a, b, towards Open a joint on one side, so that a member can be inserted from that side. Select with the joint as it was Ease a, b, play Give the joint a clearance for assembly. Select with the joint as it was

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
The temporary states of an intervention: fastenings undone and made again, members taken out and put back, the structure lifted and propped.

Operator Parameters What it does Inverse Release a, b Release a connection: undo its fastening, the members stay in contact. Secure Secure a, b Fasten a connection. Release Withdraw member, path Take a member out without destroying it, for reuse or turning. Insert Insert member, path Bring a member that is out into place along a path. Withdraw Seat member Press an inserted member fully home. Unseat Unseat member Loosen a seated member so it can be withdrawn. Seat Lift members, by Jack members up. Lower Lower members, by Lower jacked members back. Lift Prop member, at Put a temporary prop under a member. Unprop Unprop member, at Take a temporary prop away. Prop Machine member, end, joint Cut a joint into the end of a member. Fill Fill member, end Fill a machined end with new material: the shape comes back, the original material does not. Machine

docs.title: Knowledge
docs.text:
What is known about the structure. Record and Probe add knowledge and have no inverse.

Operator Parameters What it does Inverse Record text, member Record something about a member, or about the structure. none Probe member, at, finding Inspect a member at a station. none OpenUp member, what Remove a covering to expose a member and its connections. Close Close member, what Cover an opened member again. OpenUp

docs.title: intervention_grammar.approaches
docs.text:
Approaches are interventions written as compositions of operators.

Each approach looks at the model as it is when it starts and returns the operations in the order they are carried out, structure and process operators mixed. Running a program expands the approaches, so the log shows every single step and the approach it belongs to.

Where an approach needs to know which connections lie in a zone of a member, it reads the stations of the connections (the connection attribute "at"), or takes them from its zone parameter.

Classes:

  • Patch –

    Cut damaged material out of part of a member and fit a new piece.

  • Prosthesis –

    Replace a member over its full section along a length at one end.

  • MidProsthesis –

    Replace a member over its full section along a length in its middle.

  • Replacement –

    Replace a whole member.

  • Reinforcement –

    Add a piece alongside a member and fasten the two together; the piece shares the member's load path.

  • Addition –

    Introduce a new member that takes part of the load; the damage stays.

  • Reconnection –

    Remake a failed connection with a separate connector.

  • Realignment –

    Move members back into line and secure them again.

  • Subtraction –

    Take damaged or harmful material away without replacing it.

  • Repositioning –

    Take a member out, turn it, and put it back, so that its damaged parts lie where they matter less.

  • Collapse –

    Remove a bay and close the structure up (an edge ring collapse).

  • Bypass –

    Remove a member and let a neighbour that ended on it continue to the next member.

  • Lowering –

    Shorten the members standing on a base, replace the base and lower everything above onto it.

  • Retain –

    Leave the structure as it is and record why: the baseline every other approach is compared with.

docs.title: Prosthesis
docs.text:
Prosthesis(
    member,
    length,
    end="start",
    joint=None,
    zone=None,
    path="straight",
)

Bases: Approach

Replace a member over its full section along a length at one end.

Prosthesis = Release(connections in the zone) ; Split(m, s, J) ; Remove(old end) ; Add(piece) ; Insert(piece) ; Seat ; Join(J) ; Join(connections of the zone) ; Secure. The rest of the member keeps its name; the old end becomes member.old and the new piece member.new.

Parameters:

  • member (str) –

    The member whose end is replaced.

  • length (float) –

    How far the new piece reaches, measured from the end.

  • end (str, default: 'start' ) –

    "start" (default) or "end".

  • joint (dict, default: None ) –

    The joint between the remaining member and the new piece.

  • zone (list[str], default: None ) –

    Neighbours connected within the replaced length, where stations are not known.

  • path (str, default: 'straight' ) –

    How the new piece is brought in.

Source code in src/intervention_grammar/approaches.py 
def __init__(self, member, length, end="start", joint=None, zone=None, path="straight"):
    super(Prosthesis, self).__init__()
    self.member = member
    self.length = length
    self.end = end
    self.joint = joint
    self.zone = list(zone) if zone else None
    self.path = path

docs.title: MidProsthesis
docs.text:
MidProsthesis(
    member, span, joints=None, zone=None, path="straight"
)

Bases: Approach

Replace a member over its full section along a length in its middle.

MidProsthesis = Release ; Split(m, s1) ; Split(m, s0) ; Remove(segment) ; Add ; Insert ; Seat ; Join(J0) ; Join(J1) ; Join(connections of the segment) ; Secure. The two remaining pieces are member.a and member.b.

Parameters:

  • member (str) –

    The member whose middle segment is replaced.

  • span (list[float]) –

    Stations s0 and s1 of the replaced segment.

  • joints (list[dict], default: None ) –

    The joints at s0 and at s1.

  • zone (list[str], default: None ) –

    Neighbours connected within the segment, where stations are not known.

  • path (str, default: 'straight' ) –

    How the new segment is brought in, see Insert. Default "straight".

Source code in src/intervention_grammar/approaches.py 
def __init__(self, member, span, joints=None, zone=None, path="straight"):
    super(MidProsthesis, self).__init__()
    self.member = member
    self.span = list(span)
    self.joints = list(joints) if joints else [None, None]
    self.zone = list(zone) if zone else None
    self.path = path

def wall():
    r"""A timber wall of two bays without geometry.

    Sill and plate run over both bays, three posts stand between them, one rail
    in each bay, a knee brace from the first post to the plate, and a brace
    from the plate down onto the second rail. Every
    member has a type and a length, every connection a tenon, a support
    direction and the station on both members, and all joints are secured.

    ::

        plate   ======================
                |  /        |   \    |
                | /brace_1  |    \   |    brace_2
                |-----------|--------|    rail_1, rail_2
                |           |        |
        sill    ======================
             post_1      post_2    post_3

    Returns
    -------
    :class:`compas_model.models.Model`

    """
    from compas_model.models import Model

    model = Model(name="wall")
    members = [
        ("sill", "sill", 3.0),
        ("post_1", "post", 2.2),
        ("post_2", "post", 2.2),
        ("post_3", "post", 2.2),
        ("rail_1", "rail", 1.4),
        ("rail_2", "rail", 1.4),
        ("plate", "top", 3.0),
        ("brace_1", "brace", 0.85),
        ("brace_2", "brace", 1.15),
    ]
    for name, kind, length in members:
        add_element(model, name, type=kind, length=length, grounded=(name == "sill"))

    def join(a, b, sa, sb, carried, carrier):
        add_connection(model, a, b, joint=dict(TENON), state="secured", at={a: sa, b: sb}, support=[carried, carrier])

    for post, s in (("post_1", 0.1), ("post_2", 1.5), ("post_3", 2.9)):
        join(post, "sill", 0.0, s, post, "sill")
        join(post, "plate", 2.2, s, "plate", post)
    join("rail_1", "post_1", 0.0, 1.1, "rail_1", "post_1")
    join("rail_1", "post_2", 1.4, 1.1, "rail_1", "post_2")
    join("rail_2", "post_2", 0.0, 1.1, "rail_2", "post_2")
    join("rail_2", "post_3", 1.4, 1.1, "rail_2", "post_3")
    join("brace_1", "post_1", 0.0, 1.6, "brace_1", "post_1")
    join("brace_1", "plate", 0.85, 0.7, "plate", "brace_1")
    join("brace_2", "plate", 0.0, 2.3, "plate", "brace_2")
    join("brace_2", "rail_2", 1.15, 0.6, "brace_2", "rail_2")
    return model

def original_share(model):
    """Share of the members that are original fabric.

    Weighted by length where every member has one, otherwise counted. Cut
    regions are not subtracted: without geometry their volume is not known.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : :class:`compas_model.models.Model`
        A state of the structure.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Between 0 and 1. Missing members are left out.

    """
    members = [n for n in names(model) if attribute(model, n, "placement") != "missing"]
    if not members:
        return 0.0
    lengths = [attribute(model, n, "length") for n in members]
    weights = lengths if all(x is not None for x in lengths) else [1.0] * len(members)
    original = sum(w for n, w in zip(members, weights) if attribute(model, n, "fabric") == "original")
    return original / sum(weights)

    out = []

def steps(model, operations):
    """Apply operations to a copy of the model, one primitive step at a time.

    Approaches are expanded when they are reached, so each step is one
    operation that is not an approach.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : :class:`compas_model.models.Model`
        The model. It is copied and stays unchanged.
    operations : list[:class:`Operation`]
        The program: operations and approaches, in order.

    Yields
    ------
    tuple
        ``(operation, approach, before, after)``: the operation, the innermost
        approach it belongs to (or None), and copies of the model before and
        after it.

    Raises
    ------
    InterventionError
        With the step number and the operation, if one cannot be applied.

    """
    current = model.copy()
    pending = [(op, None) for op in operations]
    number = 0
    while pending:
        op, parent = pending.pop(0)
        if isinstance(op, Approach):
            pending[0:0] = [(sub, op) for sub in op.operations(current)]
            continue
        number += 1
        after = current.copy()
        try:
            op.check(after)
            op.apply(after)
        except InterventionError as error:
            raise InterventionError("step {}, {!r}: {}".format(number, op, error))
        yield op, parent, current, after
        current = after

def run(model, operations):
    """Apply a program to a copy of the model and keep every state.

    The model itself is left unchanged. Each state carries the log of the
    steps so far: ``model.graph.attributes["log"]`` lists every step, and the
    attribute "log" of each element the numbers of the steps that changed it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : :class:`compas_model.models.Model`
        The model. It is copied and stays unchanged.
    operations : list[:class:`Operation`]
        The program: operations and approaches, in order.

    Returns
    -------
    list[:class:`compas_model.models.Model`]
        The model before the first step and after every step.

    """
    states = [model.copy()]
    log = list(model.graph.attributes.get("log") or [])
    for op, parent, before, after in steps(model, operations):
        number = len(log) + 1
        entry = {
            "step": number,
            "operation": type(op).__name__,
            "layer": op.layer,
            "text": repr(op),
            "data": op.__data__,
            "approach": repr(parent) if parent is not None else None,
        }
        log.append(entry)
        after.graph.attributes["log"] = list(log)
        for name in changed(before, after):
            if name in names(after):
                set_attribute(after, name, "log", attribute(after, name, "log") + [number])
        states.append(after)
    return states

def inverse(model, operations):
    """The operations that undo a program, in the order they are carried out.

    Knowledge operations have no inverse and are left out.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : :class:`compas_model.models.Model`
        The model the program starts from.
    operations : list[:class:`Operation`]
        The program: operations and approaches, in order.

    Returns
    -------
    list[:class:`Operation`]
        The inverse of every step, last step first.

    """
    undo = []
    for op, parent, before, after in steps(model, operations):
        back = op.inverse(before)
        if back is not None:
            undo.insert(0, back)
    return undo

def changed(before, after):
    """Names of the elements whose state differs between two models.

    Parameters
    ----------
    before : :class:`compas_model.models.Model`
        The earlier state.
    after : :class:`compas_model.models.Model`
        The later state.

    Returns
    -------
    list[str]
        Elements that are new or changed in ``after``, then elements that are gone.

    """
    a, b = snapshot(before), snapshot(after)
    out = [n for n in b if n not in a or a[n] != b[n]]
    out += [n for n in a if n not in b]
    return out

docs.title: intervention_grammar.state
docs.text:
The state of a structure under intervention, kept on a compas_model Model.

Elements are the members of the structure, interactions are their connections. The state lives on the model's graph: one set of attributes per element node, one per connection edge. Element classes stay untouched, so the same operations run on any compas_model element, for example the beams of a compas_timber TimberModel.

Every operation changes the model only through the functions below. They are the six basic edits (add or remove an element, add or remove a connection, set an attribute on either) plus the lookups they need. Moving the grammar to another kind of model means translating this module and nothing else.

Element attributes

fabric      "original" or "new"
condition   "sound" or "damaged"
placement   "in" (in place), "inserted" (in place, not yet seated),
            "out" (taken out, kept) or "missing" (known, not there)
type        the role of the member, any name
grounded    True if it stands on the ground
length      in metres, if known
trim        change of length at each end, {"start": d, "end": d}
turn        {"reversed": bool, "quarter": 0..3}
offset      sum of the moves, [x, y, z]
lift        how far it is jacked up
props       stations of temporary props
cuts        regions cut out of it
ends        joints machined into its ends, {"start": joint, "end": joint}
fills       ends filled with new material after machining
findings    results of probes
notes       records
exposed     True while it is opened up
log         numbers of the steps that changed it

Connection attributes

joint       description of the joint, a dict (family and parameters)
state       "secured", "released" or "open" (made, not yet fastened)
at          station of the connection on each member, {name: station}
node        name of the point where it meets other connections
support     (carried, carrier) or "both", if known

def snapshot(model, skip=("log",)):
    """The state as plain data, for comparing two states.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : :class:`compas_model.models.Model`
        The model.
    skip : tuple[str], optional
        Element attributes left out. Default: the log.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``{name: (attributes, {neighbour: connection attributes})}``.

    """
    out = {}
    for name in names(model):
        values = {k: v for k, v in attributes(model, name).items() if k not in skip}
        links = {}
        for other in neighbours(model, name):
            links[other] = connection_attributes(model, name, other)
        out[name] = (values, links)
    return out

docs.title: intervention_grammar.structure_operators
docs.text:
Structure operators change what the finished structure is: its members, their connections, their lengths and their positions.

Collapse and Bypass, which combine several structure operators, are in intervention_grammar.approaches.

Classes:

  • Cut –

    Cut material out of a member.

  • Inlay –

    Fit a new piece into a member.

  • Split –

    Cut a member through at a station; the two pieces meet in a joint.

  • Merge –

    Make two connected pieces one member again.

  • Join –

    Join two members with a joint.

  • Unjoin –

    Take away the connection between two members.

  • Trim –

    Shorten a member at one end.

  • Extend –

    Lengthen a member at one end.

  • Turn –

    Turn a member that is out: end for end, or about its own axis.

  • Add –

    Add a member to the structure.

  • Remove –

    Take a member out of the structure for good; its connections go with it.

  • Double –

    Add a piece alongside a member, sharing its load path.

  • Support –

    Give a member a permanent support from the ground.

  • Reroute –

    Connect a member to another one instead.

  • SplitNode –

    Let some connections of a crowded node meet in a node of their own.

  • MergeNodes –

    Let the connections of two nodes meet in one.

  • Move –

    Move members permanently.

  • Swap –

    Two members that are out exchange their places in the structure.
